pr.title: Fix ICE when validating transmuting ZST to inhabited enum
pr.description:
MIR validation attempts to determine the number of bytes needed to represent the size of the source type to compute the discriminant for the inhabited target enum. For a ZST source, there is no source data to use as a discriminant so no proper runtime check can be generated.

Since that should never be possible, insert a delayed bug to ensure the problem has been properly reported to the user by the type checker.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#145786
pr.author: samueltardieu

processing.reason: PR 145791 / issue 145786 is a compiler ICE fix, not a miscompilation. The changed CheckEnums logic only triggers while validating MIR for `std::mem::transmute::<(), Enum>(())`, which the type checker rejects with E0512 because a ZST source (0 bits) cannot be transmuted to an inhabited enum (non-zero size). There is therefore no valid concrete input that Miri can execute: a corrected ZST-to-inhabited-enum transmute cannot even pass type checking, and the historical failure mode is an internal compiler panic/delayed bug ("Found discriminant with invalid size, has 0 bytes"), not a different runtime value. Modeling it as an ordinary Rust function would require fabricating an unrelated panic-versus-return rewrite (or an arbitrary return-value change), which the task forbids. No source-grounded original/incorrect pair can be validated by differential Miri execution.

evidence: Fix ICE when validating transmuting ZST to inhabited enum
MIR validation attempts to determine the number of bytes needed to represent the size of the source type to compute the discriminant for the inhabited target enum.
For a ZST source, there is no source data to use as a discriminant so no proper runtime check can be generated.
Since that should never be possible, insert a delayed bug to ensure the problem has been properly reported to the user by the type checker.
ICE: `Found discriminant with invalid size, has 0 bytes`
It is never valid to use a ZST as a discriminant for an inhabited enum, but that will
have been caught by the type checker. Do nothing but ensure that a bug has been signaled.
cannot build enum discriminant from zero-sized type
Do not attempt to take the discriminant as the source
converted to a `u128`, that won't work for ZST.
error[E0512]: cannot transmute between types of different sizes, or dependently-sized types
analysis.incorrectTransformation: When `op_size.bytes() == 0` (the source operand is a zero-sized type), the old CheckEnums path still fell through to `insert_discr_cast_to_u128`, which asserts the discriminant has a valid non-zero size. The issue reports the failure as "Found discriminant with invalid size, has 0 bytes", i.e. the pass treated a ZST source as if it could supply a discriminant value. The fix intercepts `EnumCheckType::Direct { op_size, .. } | EnumCheckType::WithNiche { op_size, .. } if op_size.bytes() == 0` and instead of inserting the check emits `tcx.dcx().span_delayed_bug(source_info.span, "cannot build enum discriminant from zero-sized type")` and replaces the terminator with `TerminatorKind::Goto { target: new_block }`. This is a confirmed ICE bug fix, not an optimization.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust crate compiled with `-Zvalidate-mir` containing an unsafe transmute from a zero-sized source type to an inhabited enum, e.g. `enum A { B, C }` and `let _: A = unsafe { std::mem::transmute(()) };`. The type checker emits E0512 because sizes differ (source `()` 0 bits, target `A` 8 bits), but MIR validation must not additionally ICE while trying to derive a discriminant from the ZST source.
analysis.originalLogic: In `CheckEnums::run_pass`, for each enum check (`EnumCheckType::Direct { source_op, discr, op_size, valid_discrs }` and `EnumCheckType::WithNiche { ... }`) the pass splits the block and inserts a discriminant validity check. The size of the source operand, `op_size`, is used to cast the discriminant source to `u128`. The PR describes: "MIR validation attempts to determine the number of bytes needed to represent the size of the source type to compute the discriminant for the inhabited target enum. For a ZST source, there is no source data to use as a discriminant so no proper runtime check can be generated."
pitfalls: Do not assume every enum check has a non-zero-sized source operand; ZST sources have no data to convert into a discriminant.
The zero-size case should not panic/ICE; the type checker is responsible for reporting the invalid transmute, so the pass should only signal a delayed bug and skip generating the check.
Do not emit a runtime discriminant validity check for a ZST source, since there is no source data to inspect.
The fix covers both `EnumCheckType::Direct` and `EnumCheckType::WithNiche`, not only direct checks.
Avoid replacing the guard with a wrong unconditional rewrite of the discriminant; the correct fallback is a `Goto` to the already-split `new_block`.
preconditions: Compile with `-Zvalidate-mir` so CheckEnums runs on the offending MIR.
Use `std::mem::transmute` from a zero-sized source type such as `()` to an inhabited enum (one with multiple variants).
The source and target sizes differ, so the type checker reports E0512 but compilation continues to MIR validation, where the ZST discriminant path is hit.
analysis.summary: CheckEnums must not attempt to construct an enum discriminant check from a zero-sized source type. Before the fix, when a transmute from a ZST (e.g. `()`) to an inhabited enum reached MIR validation with `-Zvalidate-mir`, CheckEnums proceeded to build the discriminant check and `insert_discr_cast_to_u128` hit its size assertion, producing an ICE instead of only the type-checker's E0512 error.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI test under `tests/ui/mir/validate/` compiled with `//@ compile-flags: -Zvalidate-mir`. The regression test `tests/ui/mir/validate/ice-zst-as-discr-145786.rs` defines `enum A { B, C }` and does `let _: A = unsafe { std::mem::transmute(()) };`, expecting the type-checker error `ERROR cannot transmute between types of different sizes, or dependently-sized types`. Its `.stderr` expects exactly E0512 with the note `source type: `()` (0 bits)` and `target type: `A` (8 bits)`, and no ICE. A focused differential test can compare a ZST-to-enum transmute versus a correctly-sized transmute to ensure only the ZST case avoids discriminant construction and still reports E0512.
analysis.trigger: A `CheckEnums` MIR check whose source operand size is zero (`op_size.bytes() == 0`) for a `Direct` or `WithNiche` enum check, reached during optimized-MIR/validation for a program transmuting a ZST to an inhabited enum. The issue's ICE stack shows `insert_discr_cast_to_u128` called from `CheckEnums as MirPass::run_pass`.
